title: finding(contract): is a `.d.ts` that SHIPS but is unreachable from the entry and unaddressable through `exports` a PUBLISHED ACCEPT SET? — the Clause-② precedent objectui#9732 deliberately did not set
body:
Filed by the `domain:spec` @ objectui execution seat, session `session_01UanLVj6xvbS6puBCewLr8L`. ⛔ Filed as a `finding` only — grading, `domain:*` and routing are the triage seat's. ⚠️ This is a **precedent question**, not a defect: it has no wrong behaviour to point at, and answering it changes how every package in this repo is judged.

## The question

**Is a `.d.ts` that SHIPS but is unreachable from the package entry and unaddressable through `exports` a PUBLISHED ACCEPT SET?**

Concretely: when a change moves a type declaration in such a file, does it need a `Clause-②: yes` declaration and an at-tier contract review, or not?

## Where it came from, and why it was NOT answered there

Card objectui#9722 / PR objectui#9732 repaired `BulkExecutorOptions.dataSource`, which sits in `packages/plugin-grid/src/hooks/useBulkExecutor.ts`. Its `.d.ts` ships; it is not reachable from the entry. The PR declared **`Clause-②: yes`** and this seat routed the at-tier review, ⛔ **deliberately declining to settle the general question inside a p2 bug fix** — a card whose implementation discovers that the contract must move returns to the maintainer, it does not decide on the way past. The at-tier reviewer independently agreed the question deserves its own card.

## What is measured, and by whom

**Re-derived by this seat on `origin/main`**, from `packages/plugin-grid/package.json` at version `17.6.0`:

| reading | value |
|---|---|
| `files` | `["dist", "README.md", "CHANGELOG.md", "LICENSE"]` ⇒ **`dist/**` ships** |
| `exports` keys | **`["." , "./style.css"]`** — the entry and one stylesheet; ⛔ no subpath, no wildcard |
| **[LIT CTRL]** `@object-ui/types`'s `exports` keys | **12** |

⭐ The control is the point: a package in this repo **can** and **does** declare subpaths. `plugin-grid`'s single-entry shape is a **choice**, ⛔ not a repo-wide default — so the answer cannot be 「that is just how our packages are」.

**Attributed to the at-tier reviewer of objectui#9732, ⛔ NOT re-derived here** (it read the **published 17.6.0 tarball**, not a local build; this seat has no installed tarball to repeat it against, and a probe without one returns a dead-instrument zero):

- a closure walk of `dist/index.d.ts` over relative imports reaches **18** `.d.ts` files, and **excludes** both `hooks/useBulkExecutor.d.ts` and `components/BulkActionDialog.d.ts` — with lit members `ObjectGrid.d.ts` and `BulkActionBar.d.ts` inside and an absent probe outside
- out-of-package consumers of those symbols: **0**, against a lit control of 9 / 13 / 5 files in-package

⇒ its contract reading: the `exports` map is the package's **declaration** of its published surface, and an unaddressed, type-graph-unreachable `.d.ts` is **shipped bytes, not a published accept set**. Only legacy node10 resolution could deep-import it, and that is outside the declared contract.

## The two answers, and what each costs

| | **A — shipped bytes are the surface** | **B — the `exports` map is the surface** |
|---|---|---|
| a move in such a file | needs `Clause-②: yes` + an at-tier review | needs neither |
| cost | ⭐ every repair to a non-entry helper type pays a contract review, ⛔ including ones nothing outside the package can name | ⭐ the declaration follows what a consumer can actually resolve |
| risk | reviews spent on surfaces with no consumer; the gate's signal dilutes | ⚠️ a consumer on **legacy node10 resolution** CAN deep-import it, so B declares a surface that a real resolver still reaches |
| who it binds | every package in this repo, not just this one | same |

⚠️ **B's risk is the one that needs a ruling rather than a judgement**: node10 deep-import is not hypothetical, it is a resolution mode that still exists. Whether this repo declares it out of contract is a maintainer's line.

## ⛔ What this card does NOT claim

- ⛔ It does **not** say objectui#9732's `yes` was wrong. That declaration is the **rule-prescribed conservative arm** and the review is spent; re-litigating it buys nothing.
- ⛔ It does **not** propose a remedy. If the answer is B, whether `references/contract-review.md` gains a line, or `check-clause2-carriers.mjs` gains a reading of the `exports` map, is a second question.
- ⛔ **NOT MEASURED**: how many other packages in this repo ship non-entry `.d.ts` files, and how many past `Clause-②` declarations would have been answered differently. ⚠️ That census is what would tell a maintainer whether this is a recurring cost or a one-off, and it is the first thing whoever takes this card should run.

## Dedup terms

`exports map published surface` · `entry-unreachable d.ts` · `Clause-② shipped bytes` · `node10 deep import` · `non-entry helper type`

## Provenance

Raised by this seat while adjudicating objectui#9722's Clause-② declaration, and independently seconded by the at-tier contract reviewer of PR objectui#9732 (comment 5721821004), which measured the tarball readings above. The `package.json` readings and the `@object-ui/types` contrast control are this seat's own.
